title: Implement the ASCVD Risk Calculator with specific follow-up thresholds
recommendation: Calculate 10-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk for all adults aged 40-75 years using the ASCVD Risk Calculator. Input exact values for age, sex, race, total cholesterol, HDL cholesterol, systolic BP, BP treatment status, diabetes status, and smoking status. Implement specific follow-up thresholds: if 10-year risk is ≥7.5%, discuss statin therapy; if risk is ≥20%, consider high-intensity statin.
implementation: Integrate ASCVD calculator into EHR or use mobile app during visits. Document calculated risk in a standardized location. Create decision support tools based on risk thresholds. Schedule dedicated visits to discuss risk reduction for high-risk patients. Recalculate risk annually or after significant health changes.
expected_outcomes: More accurate targeting of statin therapy to those most likely to benefit. Reduction in cardiovascular events by 20-30% with appropriate statin use. Enhanced patient understanding of personal cardiovascular risk.
target_population: Adults aged 40-75 years without established cardiovascular disease, particularly those with risk factors such as hypertension, dyslipidemia, diabetes, or smoking.
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost risk assessment that guides resource utilization. Each cardiovascular event prevented saves approximately $18,000-$30,000 in direct healthcare costs.

title: Implement the COPD Assessment Test (CAT) with specific follow-up thresholds
recommendation: Administer the COPD Assessment Test (CAT) to all patients with COPD at diagnosis and at least annually thereafter. The 8-item questionnaire assesses symptoms on a scale of 0-5 each, with total scores ranging from 0-40. Implement specific follow-up thresholds: scores 0-9 indicate low impact (optimize bronchodilator therapy), 10-20 indicate medium impact (consider pulmonary rehabilitation), 21-30 indicate high impact (consider specialist referral), and 31-40 indicate very high impact (urgent specialist evaluation).
implementation: Incorporate CAT into routine COPD follow-up visits. Create EHR templates with built-in scoring and decision support. Develop action plans based on score ranges. Schedule follow-up frequency based on CAT scores. Track scores over time to assess treatment response.
expected_outcomes: More accurate assessment of symptom burden and functional limitation. Better targeting of therapies based on disease impact. Earlier referral to specialists for high-impact disease. Improved quality of life with appropriate interventions.
target_population: All patients with diagnosed COPD, particularly those with recent exacerbations, hospitalizations, or changes in symptoms.
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost assessment that guides resource utilization. Each COPD exacerbation prevented saves approximately $7,000-$15,000 in healthcare costs.

title: Implement the BEFAST protocol for stroke recognition
recommendation: Teach patients and caregivers the BEFAST protocol for stroke recognition: Balance (sudden loss of balance), Eyes (sudden vision changes), Face (facial drooping), Arm (arm weakness), Speech (slurred speech), Time (note the time symptoms started and call 911 immediately). Have patients practice identifying these signs using role-play scenarios and provide refrigerator magnets or phone wallpapers with the BEFAST acronym.
implementation: Incorporate BEFAST education into routine visits for high-risk patients. Provide printed materials in appropriate languages. Create demonstration videos showing each sign. Conduct community education sessions. Document education in the EHR.
expected_outcomes: Faster recognition of stroke symptoms with average time-to-call reduced by 15-30 minutes. Increased emergency calls for true stroke symptoms. Improved outcomes through earlier intervention.
target_population: All adults, with priority for those with stroke risk factors (hypertension, atrial fibrillation, diabetes, previous stroke/TIA, smoking) and their caregivers.
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost education with high return on investment. Each minute saved in stroke treatment prevents loss of 1.9 million neurons and saves approximately $1,000 in long-term care costs.

title: Implement the ABCDE bundle for delirium prevention
recommendation: Implement the ABCDE bundle for hospitalized older adults: Assess for pain and manage appropriately, Both spontaneous awakening and breathing trials daily, Choice of sedation minimized, Delirium assessed using CAM or CAM-ICU daily, Early mobility and exercise. For the mobility component, assist patients to get out of bed and walk three times daily, even if only for a few minutes, unless medically contraindicated.
implementation: Create standardized order sets incorporating all bundle elements. Train all staff on delirium assessment using CAM. Develop mobility protocols with physical therapy. Document bundle completion in a standardized location. Conduct daily interdisciplinary rounds to review adherence.
expected_outcomes: Reduction in delirium incidence by 30-50%. Decreased duration of mechanical ventilation by 2-4 days. Reduced ICU and hospital length of stay by 1-3 days. Improved functional outcomes at discharge.
target_population: Hospitalized adults aged 65+ years, particularly those in intensive care units or with risk factors for delirium (dementia, severe illness, multiple medications, sensory impairments).
cost_effectiveness: Moderate implementation costs offset by substantial savings. Each case of delirium prevented saves approximately $8,000-$20,000 in healthcare costs.

title: Implement the STOP-BANG screening for sleep apnea
recommendation: Screen for obstructive sleep apnea using the STOP-BANG questionnaire: Snoring loudly, Tired during the day, Observed stopping breathing during sleep, high blood Pressure, BMI >35 kg/m², Age >50 years, Neck circumference >40 cm (16 inches), and male Gender. Score 1 point for each positive item. Implement specific follow-up thresholds: scores 0-2 indicate low risk (general sleep hygiene education), 3-4 indicate intermediate risk (consider home sleep testing), and 5-8 indicate high risk (refer for comprehensive sleep evaluation).
implementation: Incorporate STOP-BANG into health risk assessments. Measure and document neck circumference during vital signs. Create EHR templates with built-in scoring and decision support. Establish referral pathways to sleep medicine. Schedule follow-up to ensure completion of sleep testing.
expected_outcomes: Identification of obstructive sleep apnea with 84-96% sensitivity for moderate to severe disease. Improved management of comorbid conditions (hypertension, diabetes, heart failure). Reduced cardiovascular events with appropriate treatment.
target_population: Adults with risk factors for sleep apnea, including obesity, resistant hypertension, atrial fibrillation, heart failure, type 2 diabetes, or excessive daytime sleepiness.
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost screening that guides resource utilization. Each case of severe sleep apnea treated saves approximately $3,000-$5,000 annually in healthcare costs from prevented complications.

title: Implement the CAGE-AID screening for substance use
recommendation: Screen for substance use disorders using the CAGE-AID questionnaire, asking these exact questions: 1) 'Have you ever felt you ought to Cut down on your drinking or drug use?', 2) 'Have people Annoyed you by criticizing your drinking or drug use?', 3) 'Have you ever felt bad or Guilty about your drinking or drug use?', 4) 'Have you ever had a drink or used drugs first thing in the morning to steady your nerves or get rid of a hangover (Eye-opener)?' Score 1 point for each 'yes' response and implement specific follow-up: scores 1-2 warrant brief intervention, scores ≥3 warrant comprehensive assessment.
implementation: Incorporate CAGE-AID into annual wellness visits. Create EHR templates with built-in scoring and decision support. Train providers in brief intervention techniques. Establish referral pathways to addiction treatment. Schedule follow-up within 2-4 weeks for positive screens.
expected_outcomes: Identification of substance use disorders with 70-85% sensitivity. Earlier intervention for problematic substance use. Reduced progression to severe substance use disorders with appropriate intervention.
target_population: All adult patients, with annual screening recommended. Higher-risk populations include those with mental health conditions, chronic pain, history of trauma, or family history of substance use disorders.
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost screening with high return on investment. Each $1 spent on screening and brief intervention saves approximately $4-$7 in healthcare and social costs.

title: Implement the CRAFFT screening for adolescent substance use
recommendation: Screen adolescents for substance use using the CRAFFT questionnaire, asking these exact questions: 1) 'Have you ever ridden in a Car driven by someone (including yourself) who was high or had been using alcohol or drugs?', 2) 'Do you ever use alcohol or drugs to Relax, feel better about yourself, or fit in?', 3) 'Do you ever use alcohol or drugs while you are by yourself (Alone)?', 4) 'Do you ever Forget things you did while using alcohol or drugs?', 5) 'Do your Family or Friends ever tell you that you should cut down on your drinking or drug use?', 6) 'Have you ever gotten into Trouble while you were using alcohol or drugs?' Score 1 point for each 'yes' response and implement specific follow-up: scores 0-1 warrant positive reinforcement, scores ≥2 warrant brief intervention and consideration of further assessment.
implementation: Incorporate CRAFFT into adolescent well visits. Ensure confidentiality during screening. Create EHR templates with built-in scoring and decision support. Train providers in adolescent-specific brief intervention techniques. Establish referral relationships with adolescent substance use treatment programs.
expected_outcomes: Identification of problematic substance use with 80-90% sensitivity. Earlier intervention for at-risk adolescents. Reduced progression to substance use disorders with appropriate intervention.
target_population: Adolescents aged 12-21 years, with annual screening recommended for all adolescents regardless of presenting complaint.
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost screening with high lifetime return on investment. Each case of adolescent substance use disorder prevented saves approximately $50,000-$120,000 in lifetime healthcare and social costs.

title: Implement the HEADSS assessment for adolescent psychosocial screening
recommendation: Conduct a comprehensive psychosocial assessment of adolescents using the HEADSS framework, asking specific questions about: Home environment ('Who lives with you? How do you get along with each person?'), Education/Employment ('How is school going? What are your grades like? Any recent changes?'), Activities ('What do you do for fun? Who do you hang out with?'), Drugs/Alcohol ('Have any of your friends tried alcohol or drugs? Have you?'), Sexuality ('Are you attracted to boys, girls, or both? Are you in a relationship? Are you sexually active?'), and Suicide/Depression ('How is your mood? Have you ever felt so bad that life didn't seem worth living?'). Document specific concerns in each domain and develop targeted follow-up plans.
implementation: Schedule longer visits for adolescent well care. Ensure confidentiality and speak with adolescents alone. Create EHR templates for structured documentation. Develop protocols for positive findings in each domain. Establish referral relationships with adolescent-specific resources.
expected_outcomes: Identification of psychosocial concerns with 75-85% sensitivity. Earlier intervention for mental health, substance use, and social problems. Enhanced therapeutic alliance with adolescent patients.
target_population: Adolescents aged 12-21 years, with comprehensive assessment recommended annually and abbreviated assessment at problem-focused visits.
cost_effectiveness: Moderate time investment offset by early identification of high-cost problems. Each case of adolescent depression identified and treated early saves approximately $7,000-$10,000 in healthcare costs.

title: Implement the IPOS-Renal symptom assessment
recommendation: Administer the IPOS-Renal symptom assessment to all patients with stage 4-5 chronic kidney disease or on dialysis. The 17-item questionnaire assesses symptom severity on a 0-4 scale. Focus particularly on the five most common symptoms: fatigue, poor mobility, drowsiness, pruritus, and pain. For any symptom rated ≥3 (severely affecting daily life), implement a specific management plan and reassess within 2 weeks.
implementation: Incorporate IPOS-Renal into routine nephrology visits. Create EHR templates with built-in scoring and decision support. Develop symptom management protocols for common symptoms. Schedule dedicated symptom management follow-up visits. Track symptoms over time to assess treatment response.
expected_outcomes: Improved identification of burdensome symptoms with 85-95% sensitivity. Better quality of life with targeted symptom management. Reduced emergency department visits for symptom crises.
target_population: Adults with stage 4-5 chronic kidney disease (eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73m²) or receiving dialysis.
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost assessment that improves quality of life and reduces emergency care. Each emergency department visit prevented saves approximately $1,200-$1,800 in healthcare costs.

title: Implement the MUST tool for malnutrition screening
recommendation: Screen for malnutrition using the Malnutrition Universal Screening Tool (MUST): 1) Calculate BMI and score (>20 = 0, 18.5-20 = 1, <18.5 = 2), 2) Assess unplanned weight loss in past 3-6 months and score (<5% = 0, 5-10% = 1, >10% = 2), 3) Assess acute disease effect (if patient is acutely ill and has had no nutritional intake for >5 days, score 2), 4) Add scores for total risk: 0 = low risk (routine care), 1 = medium risk (observe and reassess in 3 days), ≥2 = high risk (implement nutrition care plan and refer to dietitian).
implementation: Incorporate MUST into admission assessments and weekly monitoring. Ensure accurate height and weight measurements. Create EHR templates with built-in scoring and decision support. Develop nutrition care protocols based on risk level. Establish clear referral pathways to dietitians.
expected_outcomes: Identification of malnutrition risk with 80-96% sensitivity. Earlier nutritional intervention for at-risk patients. Reduced complications and length of stay with appropriate nutritional support.
target_population: All hospitalized adults and outpatients with chronic conditions, particularly older adults, those with cancer, gastrointestinal disorders, or recent weight loss.
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost screening that prevents costly complications. Each case of malnutrition prevented or treated early saves approximately $2,000-$5,000 in healthcare costs.
